date: last-modified
pagetitle: "Extract diagnoses from LPR2 and LPR3 in R"
description: "R code to extract diagnoses from the Danish National Patient Register (LPR2 and LPR3): one or several outcomes, a reusable function and one row per person."
---

This page has the code for pulling diagnoses out of LPR: for one outcome, for
several outcomes at once, and as a reusable function, `get_lpr_diagnoses()`,
that the later pages call. You need it whenever an outcome, an exposure or a
comorbidity is defined by hospital diagnoses. When you are done you have one
table with `pnr`, contact date and ICD code from LPR2 and LPR3 combined, and you
know how to reduce it to one row per person.

Read [Understand LPR](understand-lpr.qmd) first. The code relies on what that
page explains: the two periods (LPR2 and LPR3), the D-prefix, the diagnosis
types (A/B/G) and the filter for retracted diagnoses. The extraction pattern
itself (open lazily, filter, `collect()`) is the one from [Phase
5](extraction-step-by-step.qmd) and [Phase 6](first-extraction.qmd), applied to
each LPR period.

The examples assume you already have a cohort: `cohort`, a data.frame with `pnr`
and `index_date` per person, built in [Phase
10](build-study-population.qmd). That phase comes later and uses the pattern you
learn here, so read them in order and come back to this code once your cohort
exists. They also use `inner_join()` and `bind_rows()`, explained in [Phase
12](data-manipulation.qmd).

## Before you run the code {#before-you-run}

**Check the column names in your own delivery.** The examples use the names the
registers typically have, but LPR_A renamed a number of them, and [what you were
given is not what the register
contains](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr-is-split-into-two-periods). List them with
[`arrow::schema()`](function-guide.qmd#arrow-schema), and look the confirmed
ones up in [Overview of registers](register-reference.qmd).

**Three facts from [Understand LPR](understand-lpr.qmd) that the code depends
on.** Use the LPR_A files and filter them with `lprindberetningssystem ==
"LPR3"` ([why](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr-a-format)), read LPR2's open contacts as
well as `lpr_adm` ([why](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr2-open-contacts)), and expect a
spike in diagnosis counts around 2019-2020 if your analysis counts diagnoses or
looks at trends ([why](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr3-spike)).

::: {#lpr3-filter-caveat .callout-warning}
**Check that your LPR2 files reach the end of March 2019 before you rely on the
`lprindberetningssystem == "LPR3"` filter.** The filter solves one confirmed
problem: `lpr_a_kontakt` also holds older LPR2 contacts, which would be counted
twice if you did not filter them out. It does not guarantee that your combined
series has no gap around the transition. DST's LPR2 files end on 31 March 2019,
but the files in your own delivery can end earlier.

Check it before you rely on a count that spans the transition:

```r
read_register("lpr_adm") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  summarise(max_date = max(d_inddto, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  collect()
```

If that date reaches the end of DST's own LPR2 files (31 March 2019; the regions
switched their reporting to LPR3 on 2-3 February or 2-3 March 2019, see
[Understand LPR](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr-is-split-into-two-periods)), the
filter is safe as written. If it does not, do not drop the
`lprindberetningssystem` filter to get the gap back: that reintroduces the
duplicates it exists to remove. See [DARTER pitfalls,
3](darter-pitfalls.qmd#lpr3-lprindberetningssystem) for one worked fix (a
date cutover instead of a blanket filter). The same check applies to any other
register that changed system or format during your study period.
:::

### Private hospitals are in a separate register {#private-hospitals}

Private hospitals and clinics report to a separate system, MiniPas, which
Sundhedsdatastyrelsen documents as a register of its own, [MiniPas -
LPR](https://www.esundhed.dk/Dokumentation/DocumentationExtended?id=19),
covering 2002 onwards. At DST the corresponding registers are `priv_adm`,
`priv_diag` and their satellites (2002 to 31 March 2019, [DST's register
overview](https://www.dst.dk/extranet/forskningvariabellister/Oversigt%20over%20registre.html)).
They are not part of `lpr_adm` and `lpr_diag`, and this page does not extract
them. The exception is a small group of private or association-owned hospitals
(mainly hospices) that report to LPR itself ([Sundhedsdatastyrelsen's LPR
documentation](https://www.esundhed.dk/Dokumentation/DocumentationExtended?id=5)).

If your study needs private-hospital diagnoses from before 2019, check that the
`priv_*` registers are in your delivery. They do not appear by filtering LPR2 or
LPR3 differently. `lpr_a_kontakt` holds MiniPas rows under
`lprindberetningssystem == "MiniPAS"`, but only for contacts that ended in 2017
or later ([DST's remark on
LPR_A_KONTAKT](https://www.dst.dk/extranet/ForskningVariabellister/Bemaerkning/LPR_A_KONTAKT%20-%20Landspatientregistret%20%28LPR3%29%20-Kontaktoplysninger%20omkring%20de%20enkelte%20kontakter.html)),
not the full register.

## One outcome or several: choose the route {#fetch-diagnoses-from-lpr}

Which code you use depends on how many outcomes your study has:

- **One outcome** (or a couple): filter on your ICD codes inside the query, so
  only the matching rows are read. That is the worked example below.
- **Several outcomes:** pull all A and B diagnoses once into a table called
  `all_dx`, then filter that table per outcome. It is the same code with three
  small changes, see [Several outcomes at once](#several-outcomes). You query
  LPR once instead of scanning the registers again for each outcome, and the
  function [`get_lpr_diagnoses()`](#reusable-function) does it in one call.

Either way the shape is the same, and it follows from [how LPR is
built](understand-lpr.qmd#contact-and-diagnosis-tables): a hospital contact's
`pnr` and date are in one table and the ICD code in another, so every extract is
a join between a contact register and a diagnosis register, done once per LPR
period and then stacked.

The examples use `read_register("name")` (fastreg); without fastreg use
`open_dataset("path/to/<register>/")`. LPR is one of the largest registers, so
it must be in parquet: reading it from SAS pulls the whole thing into RAM.
Convert first if nobody has: [Parquet and
fastreg](parquet-and-fastreg.qmd#convert-sas-to-parquet).

The code filters to your cohort with `semi_join(tibble(pnr = ...))` rather than
`filter(pnr %in% ...)`, because it pushes down into Arrow/DuckDB better and needs
no `!!` - see [`semi_join()`](function-guide.qmd#semi-join). You still need `!!`
for a local code list inside `filter()`, e.g. `substr(c_diag, 2, 4) %in% !!CODES`.
`CODES` must then hold three-character codes. The left side is always three
characters, so a four-character code such as `E119` silently matches nothing:
filter on `E11` and narrow afterwards on the full `c_diag`.

## One outcome: filter on your codes {#one-outcome}

The example fetches diabetes mellitus (E10-E14). Replace `CODES_REGEX` with your
own codes. It runs in four steps: one per LPR table set, then the combine.

**Setup.** The cohort's `pnr` and the codes you are looking for:

```r
library(fastreg) # read_register - read a register by name
library(arrow)   # open_dataset - fallback without fastreg
library(dplyr)

cohort_pnrs <- unique(cohort$pnr)
CODES_REGEX <- "^DE1[0-4]"   # diabetes mellitus (E10-E14) - with D-prefix
```

### Step 1: LPR2 somatic {#step-1-lpr2-somatic}

`lpr_adm` + `lpr_diag`, up to March 2019. This is the shape all three steps
follow: open both tables, keep your cohort, take
`pnr` + key + date from the contact register, join the diagnosis register on the
contact key, and only then `collect()`.

```r
lpr_adm  <- read_register("lpr_adm")  %>% rename_with(tolower)
lpr_diag <- read_register("lpr_diag") %>% rename_with(tolower)

lpr2_dm <- lpr_adm %>%
  semi_join(tibble(pnr = cohort_pnrs), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%   # ONLY your cohort. OMIT this line if you want the WHOLE population
  select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%  # d_inddto is RENAMED to date_contact (see below)
  inner_join(
    lpr_diag %>%                                    # diagnosis register: has recnum + ICD code, but neither pnr nor date
      filter(c_diagtype %in% c("A", "B"),           # A + B = action/secondary diagnoses; add "G" if you also want underlying conditions
             grepl(CODES_REGEX, c_diag)) %>%         # keep only your codes - filter BEFORE collect (D-prefix in the regex)
      select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
    by = "recnum"                                   # recnum = the key linking contact and diagnosis in LPR2
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%                                      # ONLY here is data pulled into RAM (everything above runs in the database)
  mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))                # strip the D-prefix: "DE11" -> "E11"
```

#### LPR2 contacts that never closed {#step-1-open-contacts}

`uaf_adm` + `uaf_diag`. A contact that was never closed, for example one still open
after the switch to LPR3, is not in `lpr_adm` at all, only in the open-contact
tables ([why](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr2-open-contacts)). Same shape as above, with one
addition: read only the **last year** of the open tables, because a contact
that is open for several years is in each of them.

```r
uaf_adm  <- read_register("uaf_adm")  %>% rename_with(tolower)
uaf_diag <- read_register("uaf_diag") %>% rename_with(tolower)

uaf_last_year <- uaf_adm %>%                        # the last year of the open tables (2019 in DST's files)
  summarise(last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  collect() %>%
  pull(last_year)

lpr2_open_dm <- uaf_adm %>%
  filter(year == !!uaf_last_year) %>%               # ONLY the last year: the contacts still open when DST took its copy
  semi_join(tibble(pnr = cohort_pnrs), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
  select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%  # d_inddto = the date the contact started
  inner_join(
    uaf_diag %>%
      filter(year == !!uaf_last_year,               # the same year on the diagnosis table
             c_diagtype %in% c("A", "B"),
             grepl(CODES_REGEX, c_diag)) %>%
      select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
    by = "recnum"
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))
```

Reading only the last year is what keeps a contact from being counted twice:
those contacts had not ended when DST's copy was made, so none of them is in
`lpr_adm`. Two things have to hold for that:

- **Your `lpr_adm` reaches the same year.** Check with `lpr_adm %>%
  summarise(last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% collect()`. If the two
  differ, read [Understand LPR](understand-lpr.qmd#lpr2-open-contacts) before
  you combine more years.
- **`uaf_adm` and `uaf_diag` are split by year.** `count(uaf_adm, year) %>%
  collect()` should show one row per year. A single row means the column
  labels the delivery and not the year ([DST pitfalls,
  11](dst-pitfalls.qmd#year-is-not-a-date)).

If `read_register("uaf_adm")` cannot find the register, your project was not
given the open-contact tables. DST lists them as `UAF_ADM` and `UAF_DIAG`, and
you can ask DST to add them to your delivery.

### Step 2: LPR3 {#step-2-lpr3}

`lpr_a_kontakt` + `lpr_a_diagnose`, from early 2019 onwards. Same shape,
different table and column names, plus two things LPR2 does not have: the
`lprindberetningssystem` filter on both tables and the retracted-diagnosis filter.
The variable is not in every delivery - [check that you have
it](dst-pitfalls.qmd#lpr-a-not-pure-lpr3) first.

```r
lpr3_k <- read_register("lpr_a_kontakt")  %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  filter(lprindberetningssystem == "LPR3")   # keep only LPR3-system rows (avoid the LPR2 overlap)
lpr3_d <- read_register("lpr_a_diagnose") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  filter(lprindberetningssystem == "LPR3")   # same column on the diagnosis table; the join key does not carry it

lpr3_dm <- lpr3_k %>%
  semi_join(tibble(pnr = cohort_pnrs), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
  select(pnr, dw_ek_kontakt, date_contact = kont_starttidspunkt) %>%  # LPR3's date column renamed to the SAME name
  inner_join(
    lpr3_d %>%
      filter(diag_kode_type %in% c("A", "B"),
             is.na(senere_afkraeftet) | senere_afkraeftet != "Ja",  # drop withdrawn diagnoses (LPR3 only)
             grepl(CODES_REGEX, diag_kode)) %>%
      select(dw_ek_kontakt, c_diag = diag_kode, c_diagtype = diag_kode_type),  # rename LPR3 names -> same names as LPR2
    by = "dw_ek_kontakt"                               # LPR3's contact key (NOT recnum as in LPR2)
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(date_contact = as.Date(date_contact),         # the LPR3 date is a datetime -> make it a plain date
         icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))
```

### Step 3: LPR2 psychiatric, only if you need F-codes {#step-3-lpr2-psychiatric}

`t_psyk_adm` + `t_psyk_diag`. Skip this step if your outcome is not an F-code.

```r
# any_of(): rename the keys only if your delivery renamed them (v_cpr, k_recnum, v_recnum)
psyk_adm  <- read_register("t_psyk_adm")  %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>% rename(any_of(c(pnr = "v_cpr", recnum = "k_recnum")))
psyk_diag <- read_register("t_psyk_diag") %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>% rename(any_of(c(recnum = "v_recnum")))

lpr2_psyk_dm <- psyk_adm %>%
  semi_join(tibble(pnr = cohort_pnrs), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
  select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%
  inner_join(
    psyk_diag %>%
      filter(c_diagtype %in% c("A", "B"),
             grepl(CODES_REGEX, c_diag)) %>%          # same codes as above
      select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
    by = "recnum"
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))
```

### Step 4: stack the three extracts {#step-4-stack}

This works only because all three steps produced the same column names:

```r
dm_dx <- bind_rows(lpr2_dm, lpr2_open_dm, lpr2_psyk_dm, lpr3_dm)   # drop lpr2_psyk_dm if you skipped step 3
# Columns: pnr | date_contact | c_diag | c_diagtype | icd3
```

**What must match, and what you choose.** The register's own names (`pnr`,
`recnum`, `d_inddto`, `c_diag`, `c_diagtype`, `dw_ek_kontakt`,
`kont_starttidspunkt`, `diag_kode`) must be spelled exactly as they are in the
register. The names on the left of `=` inside `select()` are yours:
`date_contact` and `icd3` are chosen here, not required. LPR2's date column is
`d_inddto` and LPR3's is `kont_starttidspunkt`, so giving both the name
`date_contact` is what lets `bind_rows()` stack them in step 4. Keep those
harmonised names identical across the three extracts; the object names
(`lpr2_dm`) can be whatever you like.

**Many codes?** Build the regex instead of typing it:

```r
codes <- c("E10", "E11", "E12", "E13", "E14")
CODES_REGEX <- paste0("^D(", paste(codes, collapse = "|"), ")")
```

**F-codes (dementia, depression)?** Extend `CODES_REGEX`, e.g.
`"^DE1[0-4]|^DF0[0-3]|^DG30"`, and do not skip step 3: contacts at psychiatric
departments before 2019 are only in the psychiatric registers.

<details>
<summary>A shorter version you may meet, and three ways it goes wrong on DST data</summary>

A colleague may have shown you this shorter approach:

```r
lpr <- left_join(lpr_adm, lpr_diag, by = "RECNUM") %>%
  filter(C_DIAGTYPE == "A",
         grepl("^S72", C_DIAG)) %>%
  group_by(PNR) %>%
  filter(D_INDDTO == min(D_INDDTO)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()
```

It is shorter but has three pitfalls on DST data:

1. **D-prefix error:** `"^S72"` does not match `"DS72..."`, so it returns zero rows with no error message. Use `"^DS72"` (with D) or strip the prefix first.
2. **`left_join` instead of `inner_join`:** keeps all admissions from `lpr_adm`, including those with no matching diagnosis. Unnecessarily heavy on national registers.
3. **No pnr filter:** loads the entire population's data. Correct when building a cohort ([Phase 10](build-study-population.qmd)), not when extracting from an existing one.

</details>

## Several outcomes at once {#several-outcomes}

If your study has more than one LPR outcome, do not run the steps above once per
outcome: that scans the registers again every time. Query LPR once, keep all A
and B diagnoses in a table called `all_dx`, and filter that table per outcome.

It is the same four steps, with three changes:

1. **Drop `CODES_REGEX` and the `grepl()` line** from every step. You are no
   longer filtering on codes at the source.
2. **Name the results `lpr2_dx`, `lpr2_open_dx`, `lpr3_dx`, `lpr2_psyk_dx`**
   and combine them into `all_dx` instead of `dm_dx`. Always include the
   psychiatric step here - `all_dx` is meant to serve outcomes you have not
   thought of yet.
3. **Save it**, so later scripts reuse it rather than re-querying:
   `saveRDS(all_dx, "path/to/all_dx.rds")`.

The joins, the keys, the renames and `bind_rows()` are unchanged.

The function [`get_lpr_diagnoses()`](#reusable-function) further down this page
does those steps in one call. Define the function first, then run:

```r
# all_dx: every A and B diagnosis for the cohort (no icd_codes = no filter on codes)
all_dx <- get_lpr_diagnoses(pnr_vector = cohort_pnrs)

saveRDS(all_dx, "path/to/all_dx.rds") # later scripts reuse it instead of querying LPR again
```

`all_dx` is large: it holds every A and B diagnosis for your whole cohort in
RAM. On a big cohort, save it and work from the `.rds`, and free the memory
with `rm()` + `gc()` when you are done ([Phase
5](extraction-step-by-step.qmd)).

### From `all_dx` to one outcome: first event per person {#first-event-per-person}

`all_dx` has one row per diagnosis, so a person with five hip fracture contacts has
five rows. An analysis dataset needs one row per person, with the date of
their first qualifying diagnosis. The four lines from `group_by()` to
`ungroup()` turn one into the other. [From event log to one row per
person](#one-row-per-person) shows the other way of collapsing.

```r
library(dplyr) # filter, inner_join, group_by, arrange, slice, left_join

CODES <- c("S72")   # hip fracture (example study) - change to your outcome

outcome <- all_dx %>%
  # 1. Keep only the diagnoses that count as your outcome
  filter(icd3 %in% CODES) %>%

  # 2. Attach each person's index_date. inner_join also DROPS anyone who is not
  #    in the cohort, so this filters and adds a column in one step.
  #    Use cohort_clean here once you have excluded prevalent cases (Phase 10).
  inner_join(cohort %>% select(pnr, index_date), by = "pnr") %>%

  # 3. Keep only contacts AFTER index. This is what makes it an outcome rather
  #    than pre-existing disease. Use <= instead for a baseline covariate
  #    (convention: on or before index = prevalent, after index = outcome).
  filter(date_contact > index_date) %>%

  # 4. Reduce to the FIRST event per person:
  group_by(pnr) %>%              #    handle each person separately
  arrange(date_contact) %>%      #    oldest contact first
  slice(1) %>%                   #    keep row 1 of each person = earliest contact
  ungroup() %>%                  #    remove the grouping again (see note below)

  # 5. Rename the surviving date to something that says what it is
  select(pnr, event_date = date_contact)

# Back onto the full cohort. left_join keeps EVERYONE, so people with no
# diagnosis get NA in event_date - that is the correct value for "no event",
# and they are censored at end of follow-up rather than dropped.
result <- cohort %>%
  distinct(pnr) %>%   # one row per person, also if a pnr is in the cohort more than once
  left_join(outcome, by = "pnr")

saveRDS(result, "path/to/extract_hip_fracture.rds")   # change filename for each new outcome
```

**What `slice(1)` does.** `slice(n)` picks rows by position, not by value:
`slice(1)` keeps the first row of each group. It only means "earliest"
because `arrange(date_contact)` put the oldest first. With
`arrange(desc(date_contact))` the same `slice(1)` gives you the latest
contact instead. See [`slice()`](function-guide.qmd#slicen).

Three things to check in this block:

- **Keep the `ungroup()`:** a grouped table stays grouped, and every later
  `mutate()` or `summarise()` then operates per person instead of on the
  whole table, without telling you.
- **Ties are broken arbitrarily:** if someone has two qualifying contacts on the
  same date, `slice(1)` keeps whichever row came first. That does not matter for
  a first-event date, since the date is the same, but it does if you also keep
  columns that differ between the two rows, such as the hospital or the specific
  ICD code.
- **Repeated `pnr` in the cohort:** step 4 collapses to one row per `pnr`, and
  the final `left_join()` is on `pnr` alone. If your cohort has repeated `pnr`
  (e.g. a comparison group matched with replacement), that join can attach one
  person's event to the wrong `index_date`. See [the callout on repeated `pnr`
  on Comparison cohort](comparison-cohort.qmd#step-4---assemble-validate-and-save).

Excluding prevalent cases (people who already had the diagnosis before the index
date) happens in [Phase 10](build-study-population.qmd). Once you have
done that, use `cohort_clean` in place of `cohort` above.

Using duckplyr instead of dplyr? `union_all()` combines before `collect()` and
needs identical column names and types, so rename the LPR3 columns to the LPR2
format first.

<details>
<summary>Try it yourself: runnable example on synthetic data (local R, not DST)</summary>

::: {.callout-important}
This example requires **RStudio installed locally on your computer** - not the DST server.
The synthetic data package (`fiktive`) is not available on DST.
Download R: [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/) · Download RStudio: [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
It uses `open_dataset()` on local `synth_data/` folders; fastreg's `read_register()` is for a configured DST project, not ad-hoc local folders.
:::

The example extracts CVD diagnoses (ischaemic heart disease, ICD-10 I20–I25) from LPR2 and LPR3 combined - the same steps as above, runnable locally on synthetic data. It follows the [one-outcome route](#one-outcome): specific codes are filtered out *before* `collect()`.

The synthetic LPR data is generated with [`fiktive`](https://github.com/sara-schwartz/fiktive), which you already know from [Phase 6 - First extraction](first-extraction.qmd#preparation-install-fiktive-and-generate-synthetic-data). Phase 6 saves `bef` and `lpr_adm` only. Run the block below for the diagnosis tables. It uses the same `n`, window, and seed, so `lpr_adm` matches.

```r
# Install fiktive for the first time:
# install.packages("remotes"); remotes::install_github("sara-schwartz/fiktive")

library(fiktive)    # synthetic DST register data
library(dplyr)      # filter, select, mutate, inner_join, bind_rows
library(arrow)      # open_dataset, write_parquet

# Preparation: generate synthetic data (run only once) -------------------------
# One call, same n / window / seed as Phase 6. Child tables only join their
# parent when they share that population. LPR2 somatic contacts stop around
# 2019-03 and lpr_a_diagnose starts in 2019, so the window covers both.
schema <- load_registers_schema()
pop <- generate_background_population(n = 60, seed = 1, schema = schema)
tables <- generate_registers(
  registers = c("lpr_adm", "lpr_diag", "lpr_a_kontakt", "lpr_a_diagnose"),
  population = pop,
  schema = schema,
  from = as.Date("2015-01-01"),
  to = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  seed = 1
)

dir.create("synth_data/lpr_adm",        recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("synth_data/lpr_diag",       recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("synth_data/lpr_a_kontakt",  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("synth_data/lpr_a_diagnose", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_parquet(tables$lpr_adm,        "synth_data/lpr_adm/lpr_adm.parquet")
write_parquet(tables$lpr_diag,       "synth_data/lpr_diag/lpr_diag.parquet")
write_parquet(tables$lpr_a_kontakt,  "synth_data/lpr_a_kontakt/lpr_a_kontakt.parquet")
write_parquet(tables$lpr_a_diagnose, "synth_data/lpr_a_diagnose/lpr_a_diagnose.parquet")
```

**The path is relative to your working directory** - check with `getwd()`.
If you have already run the preparation block in [Phase 6](first-extraction.qmd), `synth_data/bef/` and `synth_data/lpr_adm/` are already saved. This page still needs `lpr_diag`, `lpr_a_kontakt`, and `lpr_a_diagnose` from the block above.

On this fixture `senere_afkraeftet` is never `"Ja"`, so the retracted-diagnosis filter below removes nothing. Keep it: that is the filter you use on real LPR3.

```r
# Extract CVD diagnoses (same four steps as above) -----------------------------
# The ICD codes we are looking for - change these to your own outcome
CVD_CODES <- c("I20", "I21", "I22", "I23", "I24", "I25")   # ischaemic heart disease

# LPR2 somatic (up to March 2019) ----------------------------------------------
lpr_adm  <- open_dataset("synth_data/lpr_adm/")  %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR2 contact table - synthetic
lpr_diag <- open_dataset("synth_data/lpr_diag/") %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR2 diagnosis table - synthetic

lpr2_cvd <- lpr_adm %>%
  select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%           # select only necessary columns
  inner_join(
    lpr_diag %>%
      filter(c_diagtype %in% c("A", "B"),                    # only action and secondary diagnoses
             substr(c_diag, 2, 4) %in% !!CVD_CODES) %>%       # !! sends the local R vector to DuckDB
      select(recnum, c_diag),                    # only join key and diagnosis code
    by = "recnum"                                             # join key in LPR2
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%                                              # HERE data is fetched into R
  mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))                        # save cleaned code as new column

# LPR3 (March 2019 and onwards) ------------------------------------------------
lpr3_k <- open_dataset("synth_data/lpr_a_kontakt/")  %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR3 contact table - synthetic
lpr3_d <- open_dataset("synth_data/lpr_a_diagnose/") %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR3 diagnosis table - synthetic

lpr3_cvd <- lpr3_k %>%
  select(pnr, dw_ek_kontakt, date_contact = kont_starttidspunkt) %>%   # dw_ek_kontakt is join key to lpr_a_diagnose
  inner_join(
    lpr3_d %>%
      filter(diag_kode_type %in% c("A", "B"),
             is.na(senere_afkraeftet) | senere_afkraeftet != "Ja",  # exclude retracted diagnoses; on this fixture the synthetic flag is never "Ja", so the filter removes nothing
             substr(diag_kode, 2, 4) %in% !!CVD_CODES) %>%   # !! sends the local R vector to DuckDB
      select(dw_ek_kontakt, c_diag = diag_kode),             # rename to c_diag for consistency with LPR2
    by = "dw_ek_kontakt"                                     # join key in LPR3
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%                                              # fetch into R
  mutate(
    date_contact = as.Date(date_contact),                    # datetime → date
    icd3         = substr(c_diag, 2, 4)                      # strip D-prefix: "DI21" → "I21"
  )

# Combine and save -------------------------------------------------------------
all_cvd <- bind_rows(lpr2_cvd, lpr3_cvd)                   # stack LPR2 and LPR3

nrow(all_cvd)                                               # check: number of diagnosis rows
length(unique(all_cvd$pnr))                                 # check: number of unique individuals
table(all_cvd$icd3)                                         # distribution across codes

saveRDS(all_cvd, "path/to/extract_cvd.rds")                # save - change path to your own folder
```

</details>

## `get_lpr_diagnoses()` - the whole pattern as one function {#reusable-function}

Everything above is the same four steps with the code list swapped. Rather than
copy them per outcome, wrap them once: `get_lpr_diagnoses()` takes the code list
as an argument and returns the combined extract. Define it at the top of your
script, or in a `functions.R` you `source()`.

Use it when you have more than one or two outcomes:

- One place to fix when a register or a column name changes, instead of one fix
  per copy
- Each outcome becomes a single call rather than ~40 lines
- It keeps the diagnosis-type column (`c_diagtype`), so you can narrow the case
  definition for a sensitivity analysis later (see [Diagnosis
  types](understand-lpr.qmd#diagtype)) without re-querying LPR

Read the four steps above first: when a column name in your delivery differs
from the one the function assumes, you need to recognise which step it belongs
to. On DARTER, [DARTER - overview and pipeline](darter-index.qmd) carries this
function already adapted, with the confirmed register names.

```r
library(fastreg) # read_register - read a register by name
library(arrow)   # open_dataset - fallback without fastreg
library(dplyr)

# Function: get_lpr_diagnoses() - reusable LPR extract -------------------------
get_lpr_diagnoses <- function(pnr_vector, icd_codes = NULL, diagtypes = c("A", "B")) {
  # Arguments:
  #   pnr_vector : your cohort's pnr, e.g. unique(cohort$pnr)
  #   icd_codes  : optional vector of ICD codes to pull, e.g. c("E11", "I50") or your
  #                own code list. Matches on the D-prefix, so both 3-char
  #                ("E11" -> all E11x) and 4-char ("I700") work.
  #                Default NULL = pull ALL diagnoses (run once, save, filter locally).
  #   diagtypes  : "A"=action, "B"=secondary, "G"=grundmorbus (LPR2 only)
  # read_register (fastreg) reads each register by name - without fastreg: open_dataset("E:/workdata/[projectnumber]/cleaned-data/parquet-registers/<register>/") %>% rename_with(tolower)

  # keep_codes() applies the icd_codes filter to EACH of the four register queries
  # below, BEFORE collect(), so only the wanted rows are pulled (that's why it appears
  # four times). icd_codes = NULL -> no filter (pull everything).
  keep_codes <- function(x) {
    if (is.null(icd_codes)) return(x)                                # NULL = pull everything
    pattern <- paste0("^D(", paste(icd_codes, collapse = "|"), ")")  # D-prefix + code (3 or 4 chars)
    x %>% filter(grepl(pattern, c_diag))
  }


  # Open registers
  lpr_adm   <- read_register("lpr_adm")   %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR2 somatic contacts
  lpr_diag  <- read_register("lpr_diag")  %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR2 somatic diagnoses
  uaf_adm   <- read_register("uaf_adm")   %>% rename_with(tolower)   # LPR2 somatic contacts still open
  uaf_diag  <- read_register("uaf_diag")  %>% rename_with(tolower)   # their diagnoses
  uaf_last_year <- uaf_adm %>% summarise(last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    collect() %>% pull(last_year)                                     # last year of the open tables
  # Some deliveries rename the psychiatric keys (v_cpr, k_recnum, v_recnum).
  # any_of() renames them if they are there and does nothing if they are not.
  psyk_adm  <- read_register("t_psyk_adm")  %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
    rename(any_of(c(pnr = "v_cpr", recnum = "k_recnum")))            # LPR2 psychiatric contacts
  psyk_diag <- read_register("t_psyk_diag") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
    rename(any_of(c(recnum = "v_recnum")))                             # LPR2 psychiatric diagnoses
  lpr3_k    <- read_register("lpr_a_kontakt")  %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
    filter(lprindberetningssystem == "LPR3")
  lpr3_d    <- read_register("lpr_a_diagnose") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
    filter(lprindberetningssystem == "LPR3")                            # same filter as the contact table

  # LPR2 somatic
  lpr2_dx <- lpr_adm %>%
    semi_join(tibble(pnr = pnr_vector), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
    select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%
    inner_join(
      lpr_diag %>% filter(c_diagtype %in% !!diagtypes) %>% select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
      by = "recnum"
    ) %>%
    keep_codes() %>% # filter to icd_codes (before collect)
    collect() %>%
    mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))                       # strip D-prefix

  # LPR2 somatic, contacts that never closed: last year of the open tables only
  lpr2_open_dx <- uaf_adm %>%
    filter(year == !!uaf_last_year) %>%
    semi_join(tibble(pnr = pnr_vector), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
    select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%
    inner_join(
      uaf_diag %>%
        filter(year == !!uaf_last_year, c_diagtype %in% !!diagtypes) %>%
        select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
      by = "recnum"
    ) %>%
    keep_codes() %>% # filter to icd_codes (before collect)
    collect() %>%
    mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))

  # LPR2 psychiatric
  lpr2_psyk_dx <- psyk_adm %>%
    semi_join(tibble(pnr = pnr_vector), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
    select(pnr, recnum, date_contact = d_inddto) %>%
    inner_join(
      psyk_diag %>% filter(c_diagtype %in% !!diagtypes) %>% select(recnum, c_diag, c_diagtype),
      by = "recnum"
    ) %>%
    keep_codes() %>% # filter to icd_codes (before collect)
    collect() %>%
    mutate(icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))

  # LPR3
  lpr3_dx <- lpr3_k %>%
    semi_join(tibble(pnr = pnr_vector), by = "pnr", copy = TRUE) %>%
    select(pnr, dw_ek_kontakt, date_contact = kont_starttidspunkt) %>%
    inner_join(
      lpr3_d %>%
        filter(diag_kode_type %in% !!diagtypes,
               is.na(senere_afkraeftet) | senere_afkraeftet != "Ja") %>%
        select(dw_ek_kontakt, c_diag = diag_kode, c_diagtype = diag_kode_type),
      by = "dw_ek_kontakt"
    ) %>%
    keep_codes() %>% # filter to icd_codes (before collect)
    collect() %>%
    mutate(date_contact = as.Date(date_contact),               # datetime → date
           icd3 = substr(c_diag, 2, 4))

  bind_rows(lpr2_dx, lpr2_open_dx, lpr2_psyk_dx, lpr3_dx) %>% # combine the four sources
    select(pnr, date_contact, c_diag, c_diagtype, icd3)      # identical columns, drop join keys (recnum/dw_ek_kontakt)
}
```

**Use the function.** One call per extraction; only `CODES` changes:

```r
cohort    <- readRDS("path/to/full_cohort.rds")
pnr_list  <- unique(cohort$pnr)

# Fetch all A and B diagnoses for the cohort once (no icd_codes = everything)
all_dx <- get_lpr_diagnoses(
  pnr_vector    = pnr_list,
  diagtypes     = c("A", "B")    # A=action, B=secondary. To also include grundmorbus, add "G" (LPR2 only): c("A", "B", "G")
)
# Returns: pnr | date_contact | c_diag | c_diagtype | icd3

# Extract one outcome from all_dx - repeat per outcome (only if you pulled ALL, i.e. no icd_codes)
CODES <- c("S72")   # hip fracture (example study)

hip_fracture <- all_dx %>%
  filter(icd3 %in% CODES) %>%
  inner_join(cohort %>% select(pnr, index_date), by = "pnr") %>%
  filter(date_contact > index_date) %>%
  group_by(pnr) %>% arrange(date_contact) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(pnr, event_date = date_contact)

result <- cohort %>% distinct(pnr) %>% left_join(hip_fracture, by = "pnr") # one row per person
saveRDS(result, "path/to/extract_hip_fracture.rds")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
**Two ways to call the function, depending on RAM.** For a few codes, pass them
via `icd_codes`: they are filtered before `collect()`, so only those rows are
pulled, e.g. `get_lpr_diagnoses(pnr_list, icd_codes = c("E11", "I50"))`. For
many different outcomes, pull everything once (omit `icd_codes`), save with
`saveRDS()`, free memory with `rm()` + `gc()` ([Phase
5](extraction-step-by-step.qmd)), then filter locally with `readRDS() %>%
filter(icd3 %in% ...)`, so you do not scan the registers again for each outcome.
:::

## From event log to one row per person {#one-row-per-person}

`get_lpr_diagnoses()` (and the extracts above) return an **event log**: many
rows per person, one per diagnosis. An analysis needs one row per person. Two patterns
turn it into one row per person:

**A) One outcome with a date** (e.g. time-to-event): filter to the codes, and
take each person's first contact, the `slice(1)` pattern above.

**B) Many binary variables at once** (e.g. comorbidity flags): build the flags,
collapse with `any()`, and merge onto the cohort. `any()` returns `TRUE` if the
person has at least one matching diagnosis in the window (0/1, not a count):

```r
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr) # replace_na

# 1. Build your flags (one expression per variable)
diagnosis_flags <- all_dx %>%
  inner_join(cohort %>% distinct(pnr, index_date), by = "pnr") %>% # attach index_date (every index date the person has)
  filter(date_contact <= index_date) %>% # on or before index only (baseline covariate)
  mutate(
    dx_diabetes = icd3 %in% c("E10", "E11"),
    dx_copd = str_detect(c_diag, "^DJ4[1-4]"),
    dx_heart_failure = str_detect(c_diag, "^DI50")
  )

# 2. Collapse to one row per person and index date: any() = at least one in that window?
#    index_date is in the grouping because the window "on or before index" is
#    different for each index date the person has.
diagnosis_flags_collapsed <- diagnosis_flags %>%
  group_by(pnr, index_date) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("dx_"), ~ as.integer(any(.))), .groups = "drop")

# 3. Merge onto the cohort; people with no diagnosis get NA -> set to 0
cohort_diagnoses <- cohort %>%
  left_join(diagnosis_flags_collapsed, by = c("pnr", "index_date")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("dx_"), ~ replace_na(., 0)))
```

It gives one 0/1 flag per comorbidity per person, ready to enter your model as
covariates. (The same `group_by(pnr, index_date) %>% summarise(any(.))` pattern
is used on the [NMI](nmi.qmd) page, for example.)

Step 2 groups on `pnr` and `index_date`, and step 3 rejoins on both. If
your cohort has one row per person, that gives the same result as `pnr` alone.
If a `pnr` is repeated (e.g. a comparison group matched with replacement),
it keeps each row's flags tied to that row's own index date, see [the callout on
repeated `pnr` on Comparison cohort](comparison-cohort.qmd#step-4---assemble-validate-and-save).

## Remove unwanted diagnoses {#clean-diagnoses}

A few codes record why a person was at the hospital rather than a disease of
their own, and are usually removed from both outcomes and comorbidity:

- **"Healthy companion":** someone admitted as a companion to another patient,
  e.g. a parent, ICD-10 `DZ763`. Related contact/observation codes with no
  disease: `DZ032`, `DZ038`, `DZ039`.

```r
all_dx <- all_dx %>%
  filter(!substr(toupper(c_diag), 1, 5) %in% c("DZ763", "DZ032", "DZ038", "DZ039"))
```

What to remove depends on your project and question: `DZ03*` (observation for
suspected disease) is genuinely relevant in some studies and should be kept
there. The pattern is adapted from [the Plana-Ripoll group's code on
OSF](https://osf.io/zhfyp/overview); verify against your own data.
